text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Increased 5xx rate on inference-east-1 (p50 latency steady). 5xx rate ~6.2% over the last 2m, errors concentrated on model-shard-42. Tagging on-call primary.

Maria R: saw this, thx. I'm primary but need to hand off in ~15m for a calendar conflict. marking this thread for handoff notes + quick remediations.

Sanjay P: FYI, I'm nearby and can take secondary duties while you swap. Any immediate customer impact?

Maria R: looks like elevated request errors to a few customer routes — not full outage but some retries. customers in EU/APAC hitting east-1 via routing. If we can fail traffic to standby or restart shard it's low-lift.

Maria R: quick checklist (doing in order):
1) confirm shard health
2) try soft restart of inference process on shard-42
3) flush KV prefix for that shard to rule out degraded cache entries
4) route small % to fallback model-group (reduced mem config) if restarts don't drop 5xx
5) if >10% errors or >5m sustained, page SRE escalation.

Liam T: I'll be able to take primary in 12m. Maria — can you paste runbook links and exact commands so I can pick up?

Maria R: yup, pinned commands below and runbook links. Follow order above.

Maria R: Commands (run as rwd-admin):
```
# check pod health for shard-42
kubectl get pods -n inference -l shard=42 -o wide

# soft restart of process (graceful)
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-shard-42 -n inference

# flush KV cache for shard prefix
rwdctl cache flush --prefix "kv:inference:shard:42"

# failover routing (canary 10%)
rwdctl routing set --route /v1/generate --from region:east-1 --to region:west-2 --weight 10
```

Maria R: expected quick checks: pods should go into Terminating -> Running within ~30s-90s for graceful restart. If pods stay CrashLoopBackOff or Pending -> escalate runbook step 4.

Maria R: runbooks: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/inference-5xx , https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-flush , https://internal.redwood/handbooks/oncall-handoff

Sanjay P: copying runbook. Quick note: if cache flush doesn't help, the issue in the past was a bad KV key causing deserialization errors — run `rwdctl cache inspect --prefix "kv:inference:shard:42" --sample 10` to see suspicious entries before blanket flush.

Maria R: good call. do that if you want to be conservative. I'm going to attempt the graceful restart now. I'll report results.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout restart started for deployment/inference-shard-42 by Maria R (rwd-admin). CI/CD link: https://ci.internal/redwood/rollouts/2345

Maria R: restart done, pods cycling. watching 5xx rate.

(30s pass)

Maria R: 5xx dropped to ~3.1% after restart, but still bumping. Initiating KV cache inspection before flush.

Sanjay P: output from inspect (sample):
```
# rwdctl cache inspect --prefix "kv:inference:shard:42" --sample 10
key: kv:inference:shard:42:user:12345 size: 12kb last-mod: 2026-03-14T02:11Z
key: kv:inference:shard:42:session:abcd size: 2kb last-mod: 2026-03-14T02:12Z
key: kv:inference:shard:42:feature:x corrupted-json
... (7 more)
```

Sanjay P: seeing a couple `corrupted-json` entries. that's suspicious. recommend targeted delete of those keys then monitor.

Maria R: agreed, do targeted delete for corrupted keys first (safer). If errors persist, do full prefix flush.

Liam T: I'll take over after your restart settles. Maria — is there anything you want me to run while you hop off?

Maria R: handoff to @Liam T in ~10m. I will leave the thread with explicit next steps:
- Primary -> Liam T (take over pager)
- Secondary -> Sanjay P (cover alerts, runbooks)
- Action items: watch 5xx and error logs, run targeted deletes for corrupted keys, escal to SRE if >10% or customer-impacting >5m

Maria R: targeted delete command example:
```
rwdctl cache delete "kv:inference:shard:42:user:12345"
```

ops-bot: automation: executed 1 cache-delete for key kv:inference:shard:42:user:12345 by Sanjay P — OK

Maria R: metrics trending downward: 5xx at 1.4% now. good sign.

Liam T: I'm now primary (taking pager). thanks Maria, @Sanjay take over secondary. I'll keep monitoring for the next hour.

Sanjay P: acknowledged, on secondary. I'll keep an eye on KV errors and proxy logs.

Maria R: thanks team, leaving for call. quick note in handoff doc: include the `--sample` inspect step before flush on next shift; we had two recoveries recently caused by bad cache entries.

Liam T: small follow-up — routing canary ready as fallback if we see another spike. Command to revert weight to 0: `rwdctl routing set --route /v1/generate --from region:east-1 --to region:west-2 --weight 0`

(10m pass)

ops-bot: metrics-bot: anomaly cleared for inference-east-1. 5xx back to baseline 0.3% over last 5m.

Liam T: closing loop — everything stable. leaving notes in handoff doc: https://internal.redwood/handbooks/oncall-handoff#2110003333. If you pick this up later, check recent cache deletes & rollouts.

Sanjay P: thanks — will add a short blurb about targeted-delete pattern.

Maria R: appreciated. :wave:

Liam T: good handoff, marking thread resolved unless someone sees regressions.

incident-bot: Incident thread auto-close check: no active pages for 30m. Marking as resolved. :white_check_mark:
